glm.feedback:
**Findings**

- Category: regression | Severity: medium
  File: `client/src/components/external/MarkdownText.tsx:89-97`
  The table wrapper is applied unconditionally in the shared `MarkdownText` component, so **every** consumer of markdown rendering (BubbleTranscript and anything else) now gets tables wrapped in a `<div class="mc-table-wrap">`. The comment claims "without touching other consumers," but the wrapper DOM change is global — existing CSS in other consumers that targets `table` via sibling/child combinators, or `td > *` selectors, can break; a `<div>` inside a `<li>` containing a table also changes layout in lists.
  Suggestion: gate the wrapper (e.g., a context/prop from the mission chat path) or verify and snapshot-test the other MarkdownText consumers.

- Category: spec | Severity: medium
  File: `client/src/styles/mission-chat.css:14-19` and `mission-operation.css:219-220`
  Hardcoded hex values (`--thead-fallback: #f5f5f4`, `--link: #7fdcca`, `--link-hover: #a6ebde`, `--thead: #2d2a28`) sit outside the established token layer the repo's `no-hardcoded-colors` test guards. The operation CSS already had literals, but the new `--thead-fallback` in mission-chat.css is a fresh hardcoded color introduced by this diff.
  Suggestion: hoist these into the shared token file (or wherever the existing dark tokens live) so the no-hardcoded-colors check passes.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: medium
  File: `client/src/styles/mission-chat.css:23-25, 32-36`
  The new scale/spacing custom properties (`--fs-chat`, `--gap-block`, etc.) are defined only on `.mc-op`, but consumers like `.mc-feed-card`, `.mc-ask-question` are styled with `var(--fs-chat)` / `var(--gap-block)` **without fallbacks**. Anywhere these classes render outside a `.mc-op` subtree (tests, storybook, other surfaces that previously relied on the literal `14px`/`16px`), the declarations become invalid-at-computed-value-time and font-size/margins silently unset (font falls back to inherited size, paragraph margins collapse to 0 — losing the spec's 12px paragraph gap there).
  Suggestion: add fallbacks (`var(--fs-chat, 15px)`) or define the tokens on a scope that provably contains every consumer.

- Category: spec | Severity: low
  File: `client/src/styles/mission-chat.css:41`
  Spec says chat links are "light teal #7fdcca, underlined". In light theme `--link` is undefined, so links fall back to `var(--info)` — light-mode chat links are not teal. This may be deliberate (teal on white is ~1.9:1 contrast), but it's a spec deviation with no record.
  Suggestion: either define a light-scope `--link` that meets contrast and note the deviation, or document the fallback choice.

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: `client/src/styles/mission-chat-scale.test.ts:20-28`
  The scale test greps the CSS source for token declarations and single-selector patterns; it would pass if the tokens were declared but never actually applied to the right elements (e.g., if `.mc-feed-card` were renamed). It validates the stylesheet text, not rendered behavior.
  Suggestion: acceptable as a guard, but pair with at least one DOM-level assertion (e.g., computed style on a rendered feed) or visual baseline per repo rules; also note the spec requires visual baselines and none are included in this diff.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
  File: `client/src/styles/mission-chat.css:49`
  `.mc-feed-card .mc-table-wrap tr:nth-child(2n) { background: transparent; }` is dead/contradictory next to the `td` zebra rule on the line above (td background wins visually, so zebra still works, but this rule reads as if it cancels zebra and will confuse future edits).
  Suggestion: delete the rule or comment why `tr` background must stay transparent.

**What's sound:** the toggle removal for text/explanation/answer is correctly implemented and the retained `detailFull` toggle matches "Show more only for raw tool data"; the `data-switch` logic and its test are correct; contrast math in the test checks out (faint #8f8981 on #1a1817 ≈ 5.1:1); test updates genuinely verify the new no-toggle behavior (a regression to the old toggle implementation would fail them).

Overall: the core behavior change is correct and well-tested, but the global MarkdownText table wrapper, the unscoped custom properties, and the hardcoded colors should be fixed before merge — ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
